audit: Independent finite visual comparison of actual saved SPAN renders; no G06 heavy array audit in this record
viewed: RELAXED_G06: front and side whole views

observations.facets: G06 resolves smaller ridges more finely than G05. The original large carrier facets remain visible; increased sampling alone does not remove them.
observations.relaxation: The bounded G03 relaxation modestly improves broad panel continuity and reduces a few distracting facet transitions. Its improvement over unrelaxed G06 is smaller than the main original-to-attached-relief change.
observations.body_connection: All three visually read as relief growing from the same body. RELAXED_G06 does not reintroduce the rejected detached branch-component appearance.
observations.valley_branch_hierarchy: Deep inherited valleys and fold roots remain readable. Fine terraces and clustered lobes are clearer, but there is still no strong continuous branching hierarchy across all scales.
observations.silhouette: Whole front and side views retain the main column proportions, upper and lower masses, deep cavities and sharp outward lips. Local corners are softened, not globally preserved exactly.
observations.remaining_risk: Several dense regions still read as thick crust or terraced surface folds. The result remains a locally height-projected detail system rather than free three-dimensional branching.

recommendation: Select RELAXED_G06 as the bounded close-detail lead; retain G05 and unrelaxed G06 as causal comparisons.
aesthetic_status: PARTIAL: modest further refinement of body-attached detail, not completion of the Hansmeyer/Digital Grotesque reference target.
limits: This review visually evaluates SPAN only; no claim of identical visual improvement on COUNTER.
Carrier relaxation and relief are separate movement budgets; their numbers are not the total displacement from original G03.
G06 topology/symmetry values here are read from saved metadata, not independently recomputed in this visual audit.
No intersection, fabrication or exact macro-fold preservation claim.
